principle: One connected knowledge base; colors are retrieval lenses, not isolated silos or permission levels.

hats.name: Red Hat
hats.boundary: Repair and diagnostics must respect ownership, safety, and device protections.

hats.name: Orange Hat
hats.boundary: Respect consent, attribution, and applicable intellectual-property constraints.

hats.name: Yellow Hat
hats.boundary: Distinguish established evidence, hypotheses, estimates, and open questions.

hats.name: Green Hat
hats.boundary: Generated code must be reviewed and tested; execution requires separate authorization.

hats.name: Blue Hat
hats.boundary: Network and infrastructure operations must use authorized assets and scoped access.

hats.name: Purple Hat
hats.boundary: Keep assistance authorized, defensive, and bounded; do not infer permission from technical access.

hats.name: Black Hat
hats.purpose: Critical thinking, risk, and failure analysis
hats.boundary: Use adversarial thinking to identify and reduce risk, not to enable harm.

hats.name: White Hat
hats.boundary: Track where claims came from; never upgrade unsupported claims to verified facts.

hats.name: Brown Hat
hats.boundary: Flag physical hazards and recommend qualified help where the risk exceeds safe guidance.

hats.name: Rainbow Hat
hats.boundary: Show which domains contributed, surface conflicting evidence, and do not hide uncertainty in a blended answer.

routing_rules: Assign one primary hat and any materially relevant secondary hats to each knowledge item.
Do not force every item into exactly one domain.
White Hat provenance and epistemic metadata apply across all hats.
Use Rainbow Hat when a task genuinely combines domains; it coordinates retrieval rather than replacing source domains.
A hat classification never grants tool permissions or execution authority.
Preserve the original source and link all extracted or normalized records to it.
When evidence conflicts, preserve both records and mark the conflict for review rather than silently choosing one.
